chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated allelic effect; linked causal variant or passenger signal
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at the variant in HCT116.
No allele-specific enhancer activity; disease association reflects LD with another causal variant or chance.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF binding at rs13078086 is reproducibly detected in HCT116 cells and tracks with an allele-specific enhancer/reporter signal.
CRISPR editing of rs13078086 T>G in HCT116 changes expression of a nearby gene in the predicted direction.

chains.title: CDX2 loss at the alt G allele reduces a 3q28 enhancer regulating TP63
chains.element: rs13078086 lies in a distal non-coding enhancer element near the 3q28 CRC risk locus; the ref T allele preserves a CDX2-binding site and the alt G allele weakens it.

links.claim: CDX2 binds the ref T allele more strongly than the alt G allele at rs13078086; QBiC-SELEX coverage for CDX2 is not_checked because no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is available in this no-evidence setting.
The variant sits in a distal enhancer element whose activity is allele-dependent, with ref T supporting stronger CDX2-dependent enhancer activity.
This enhancer regulates a nearby 3q28 target gene, most plausibly TP63 in this locus context.
The effect is cell-type dependent and detectable in HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells, where CDX2 is expressed.
Reduced CDX2-dependent enhancer activity at the alt G allele modestly increases colorectal cancer risk, consistent with the GWAS signal.

predictions: Allele-specific CDX2 ChIP or EMSA: ref T > alt G.
Reporter/STARR-seq in HCT116: ref T enhancer activity > alt G.
CDX2 knockdown reduces enhancer activity and target-gene expression in HCT116.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ChIP/EMSA shows no CDX2 binding or no T>G preference at this position.
CRISPR-editing the variant does not alter the candidate target gene or enhancer activity.
CDX2 knockdown does not reduce enhancer activity in HCT116.

chains.title: FOXA1 gain at the alt G allele activates a 3q28 enhancer near FGF12
chains.element: rs13078086 lies in a distal non-coding enhancer; the alt G allele creates or strengthens a FOXA1-binding site and increases enhancer activity.

links.claim: FOXA1 binds the alt G allele more strongly than the ref T allele at rs13078086; QBiC-SELEX coverage for FOXA1 is not_checked because no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is available.
The variant lies in a distal enhancer element whose activity is increased by the alt G allele in a FOXA1-dependent manner.
This enhancer regulates a nearby 3q28 gene, with FGF12 as an alternative candidate to TP63.
The effect is detectable in HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells, where FOXA1 is expressed.
Gain of FOXA1-dependent enhancer activity at the alt G allele modestly increases colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP or EMSA: alt G > ref T.
Reporter/STARR-seq in HCT116: alt G enhancer activity > ref T.
FOXA1 knockdown reduces alt-allele enhancer activity and target-gene expression.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ChIP/EMSA shows no FOXA1 binding or no G> T preference.
FOXA1 knockdown does not affect the candidate enhancer or target gene in HCT116.
Reporter assays show no alt-allele gain of enhancer activity.

chains.title: TFAP2A loss at the alt G allele reduces a 3q28 enhancer regulating TP63
chains.element: rs13078086 lies in a distal non-coding enhancer; the ref T allele supports stronger TFAP2A binding and enhancer activity.

links.claim: TFAP2A binds the ref T allele more strongly than the alt G allele at rs13078086; QBiC-SELEX coverage for TFAP2A is not_checked because no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is available.
The variant lies in a distal enhancer element whose activity is allele-dependent, with ref T supporting stronger TFAP2A-dependent activity.
This enhancer regulates TP63 at the 3q28 locus.
The effect is detectable in HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells, where TFAP2A is expressed.
Reduced TFAP2A-dependent enhancer activity at the alt G allele modestly increases colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific TFAP2A ChIP or EMSA: ref T > alt G.
Reporter/STARR-seq in HCT116: ref T enhancer activity > alt G.
TFAP2A knockdown reduces enhancer activity and TP63 expression in HCT116.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ChIP/EMSA shows no TFAP2A binding or no T>G preference.
TFAP2A knockdown does not alter the candidate enhancer or target gene in HCT116.
CRISPR editing does not change TP63 or nearby gene expression.

matrix.test: Allele-specific EMSA with HCT116 nuclear extract using ref-T and alt-G probes, plus anti-CDX2/anti-FOXA1 supershifts

outcomes.outcome: ref T shift stronger; anti-CDX2 supershifts
alt G shift stronger; anti-FOXA1 supershifts
ref T shift stronger; anti-TFAP2A supershifts

next_experiment: Single cheapest experiment to separate the top two chains (H0 null vs H1 CDX2): allele-specific EMSA in HCT116 nuclear extract comparing ref-T and alt-G probes, with an anti-CDX2 supershift; a clear ref-T-specific CDX2 shift supports H1, while no reproducible allele-specific shift supports H0. Adding anti-FOXA1 in the same gel also separates H2 if needed.
